title: Pulse-pressure–pulse interaction does not improve transferred handgrip prediction beyond flexible conventional measures
abstract: We tested whether a sex-specific interaction between pulse pressure and resting pulse adds predictive information for concurrent combined handgrip strength beyond flexible additive hemodynamics and body size. Models trained in NHANES 2011–2012 (n=3848) were frozen and tested in separately recruited 2013–2014 (n=4334). Target examination-weighted MSE increased from 128.3894 to 128.5488 kg², delta +0.1594; joint source/target rescaled-PSU bootstrap 95% interval [-0.3600, +1.4680]. The registered improvement criterion failed. Point MSE also worsened against a comparator including flexible systolic rate-pressure product. Small favorable MAE and subgroup differences do not establish a useful biomarker. This exploratory negative result concerns two recruitment cohorts in one survey program, not external-program validation or absence of vascular–muscle biology.
